object.title: The even Goldbach conjecture
object.statement: Let $x$ be an even natural number. **Even Goldbach conjecture.** Every even natural number $x$ can be expressed as the sum of at most two primes. This is one of the central open problems in additive number theory; numerical verification is known to very large bounds, but no proof is known in general.
object.source_name: Terence Tao, “Every odd number greater than 1 is the sum of at most five primes”, arXiv:1201.6656 (2012).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1201.6656

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2012).

object.title: Conjecture on bondage numbers of Cartesian products of paths
object.statement:
Let $P_n$ and $P_m$ be paths, and let $P_n\times P_m$ denote their Cartesian product. Write $b(\,\cdot\,)$ for the bondage number. **Path-product bondage conjecture.** For $m\geqslant5$,

$$
b(P_n\times P_m)\leqslant2.
$$

The source motivates this by the behavior of vertex removal in path products but gives no resolution.
object.source_name: Jun-Ming Xu, “On Bondage Numbers of Graphs – a survey with some comments”, arXiv:1204.4010 (2012).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1204.4010

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of April 2012). “However, Liu and Sun\, presented a counterexample to this conjecture.”

object.title: Borsuk's conjecture on partitioning sets of bounded diameter
object.statement: Let $S$ be a set of diameter $d>0$ in Euclidean $n$-space $\mathbb R^n$. **Borsuk's conjecture.** Every such set is the union of $n+1$ sets, each of diameter less than $d$. The conjecture is the classical Borsuk problem on reducing the diameter of a set by partitioning it; its resolution depends on the dimension, and the general statement is not valid in all dimensions.
object.source_name: M. Hujter and Z. Lángi, “On the multiple Borsuk numbers of sets”, arXiv:1206.0892 (2012).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1206.0892

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2012).

object.title: One-versus-t hardness conjecture for acquaintance time
object.statement:
Let $t\in\mathbb{N}$ be a constant and let $G$ be a graph. Write $\mathcal{AC}(G)$ for the acquaintance time of $G$. **One-versus-$t$ hardness conjecture.** It is $\mathcal{NP}$-hard to decide whether

$$
\mathcal{AC}(G)=1
$$

or

$$
\mathcal{AC}(G)\geq t.
$$

This is proposed as a stronger hardness result than the paper's factor-$2$ gap, and remains conjectural in the source.
object.source_name: Itai Benjamini, Igor Shinkar and Gilad Tsur, “Acquaintance Time of a Graph”, arXiv:1302.2787 (2014).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1302.2787

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2013).

object.title: Partial rainbow matching conjecture for matchings of size k
object.statement: Let $k$ matchings of size $k$ be given in a bipartite graph. A **partial rainbow matching** is a matching containing at most one edge from each given matching. **Partial rainbow matching conjecture.** These matchings possess a partial rainbow matching of size $k-1$. The paper states that this would imply the Brualdi–Stein conjecture for Latin squares.
object.source_name: Ron Aharoni, Pierre Charbit and David Howard, “On a Generalization of the Ryser-Brualdi-Stein Conjecture”, arXiv:1305.6164 (2013).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1305.6164

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of May 2013). “For even $n$ this is false, and Brualdi and Stein raised independently the following natural conjecture: In a Latin square of order $n$ there exists a partial transversal of size $n-1$.”

object.title: The gap conjecture for vertices of non-degenerate 3-way transportation polytopes
object.statement:
Let $p \times q \times s$ be a non-degenerate $3$-way transportation polytope specified by $2$-margin matrices $U,V,W$, and let $f_0(M(U,V,W))$ denote its number of vertices. **The gap conjecture.** It is impossible to have

$$
(p-1)(q-1)(s-1)+1 < f_0(M(U,V,W)) < 2(p-1)(q-1)(s-1).
$$

The conjecture is known to hold when $p,q,s \leq 3$, but its general status is not established here.
object.source_name: Jesús A. De Loera and Edward D. Kim, “Combinatorics and Geometry of Transportation Polytopes: An Update”, arXiv:1307.0124 (2013).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1307.0124

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of July 2013). “This conjecture was proved to be false in .”

object.title: Chromatic-polynomial coefficient unimodality conjecture
object.statement: Let $P$ be the chromatic polynomial of a graph. **Unimodality conjecture.** The sequence of coefficients of $P$ is unimodal. The source reports this as a long-standing conjecture from graph theory and immediately says that it was very recently proved.
object.source_name: Mikami Hirasawa and Kunio Murasugi, “Various stabilities of the Alexander polynomials of knots and links”, arXiv:1307.1578 (2013).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1307.1578

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of July 2013). “Very recently, the following long-standing conjecture was proved in .”

object.title: Reduction conjecture for interval colorings of complete tripartite graphs
object.statement:
Let $K_{k,m,n}$ be the complete tripartite graph with part sizes $k,m,n$, where $k\leq m\leq n$ and $n>k+m$. **Reduction conjecture.**

$$
K_{k,m,n}\text{ is interval colorable}\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad K_{k,m,n-k-m}\text{ is interval colorable}.
$$

This is proposed as a generalization of the $K_{1,m,n}$ colorability problem; the source gives no resolution of the reduction in this range.
object.source_name: Andrzej Grzesik and Hrant Khachatrian, “Interval edge-colorings of K_1,m,n”, arXiv:1308.4431 (2013).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1308.4431

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2013).

object.title: CoNP-completeness of balanced skew partition detection
object.statement: Let $\operatorname{BSP}$ denote the decision problem whose instance is a graph $G$ and whose question is whether $G$ has a balanced skew partition. **The balanced skew partition conjecture.** The problem $\operatorname{BSP}$ is coNP-complete. The paper establishes NP-hardness; the conjectured coNP-completeness would require the corresponding membership in coNP.
object.source_name: Nicolas Trotignon, “Decomposing Berge graphs and detecting balanced skew partitions”, arXiv:1309.0680 (2013).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1309.0680

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of September 2013).

object.title: The Eulerian conjecture for the augmented wiring-diagram poset
object.statement: Let $W_n$ be the poset of equivalence classes of lensless wiring diagrams, ordered by breaking crossings, and let $\widehat{0}$ be a new minimal element adjoined to $W_n$. **Eulerian conjecture.** The poset $W_n\cup\{\widehat{0}\}$ is Eulerian. The source states that this conjecture implies the Eulerian conjecture for $EP_n$. Its resolution is not given in the supplied text.
object.source_name: Joshua Alman, Carl Lian and Brandon Tran, “Circular Planar Electrical Networks I: The Electrical Poset EP_n”, arXiv:1309.2697 (2013).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1309.2697

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2013).

object.title: Kinser hierarchy dual-containment conjecture
object.statement:
For each integer $n>4$, let $\mathcal{K}_n$ be the class of matroids satisfying the $n$-th Kinser inequality, and let $\mathcal{K}_n^*$ denote its dual class. **Kinser hierarchy dual-containment conjecture.**

$$
\mathcal{K}_{n+1}^*\subseteq\mathcal{K}_n.
$$

This conjecture describes how the dual of each Kinser class is expected to lie inside the preceding class. The source gives no resolution.
object.source_name: Amanda Cameron, “Kinser inequalities and related matroids”, arXiv:1401.0500 (2014).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0500

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2014).

object.title: The planar subcubic spectral-radius ratio conjecture
object.statement: Let $G$ be a planar subcubic graph, and let $R(G)$ denote the ratio defined earlier in the paper. **Planar subcubic conjecture.** If $G$ is a planar subcubic graph, then $R(G)\le 1$. No planar subcubic graph with $R(G)>1$ is known, and the conjecture remains open.
object.source_name: Bojan Mohar, “Median eigenvalues and the HOMO-LUMO index of graphs”, arXiv:1401.1865 (2014).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.1865

Status: **open** according to the source (as of January 2014). “The following open problems remain unanswered: [(1)] It remains to see if $\sqrt{d}$ or $\sqrt{d-1}$ is the correct value for $R(d)$.”

object.title: The circle extension distinguishing number conjecture
object.statement:
Let $\mathbb{S}^1$ be the circle with its natural group action, and let $\operatorname{ext}_D(\mathbb{S}^1)$ denote its extension distinguishing number.

**Circle extension conjecture.**

$$
\operatorname{ext}_D(\mathbb{S}^1)=6.
$$

The paper proves the lower bound $\operatorname{ext}_D(\mathbb{S}^1)\geq 6$ and conjectures that this lower bound is sharp; the matching upper bound is left open.
object.source_name: Michael Ferrara, Ellen Gethner, Stephen G. Hartke, Derrick Stolee and Paul S. Wenger, “Extending Precolorings to Distinguish Group Actions”, arXiv:1405.5558 (2014).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1405.5558

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2014).

object.title: Edge self-amalgamation genus-distribution conjecture
object.statement: Let $(H,e,f)$ be a **doubly edge-rooted graph** with 2-valent roots $e$ and $f$. Consider the two graphs that can be formed by amalgamating the edge-roots $e$ and $f$. **Edge self-amalgamation conjecture.** The genus distributions of both resulting graphs are log-concave. This is a restricted form of the general genus-distribution log-concavity conjecture; the source gives no resolution.
object.source_name: Jonathan L. Gross, Toufik Mansour, Thomas W. Tucker and David G. L. Wang, “Log-Concavity of Combinations of Sequences and Applications to Genus Distributions”, arXiv:1407.6325 (2014).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1407.6325

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of July 2014). “One of the genus polynomials of these graphs was proved to have non-real zeros in .”

object.title: Points-Lines-Planes conjecture for Whitney numbers of rank-four matroids
object.statement:
Let $M$ be a rank-four matroid, and let $W_k$ denote the number of flats of $M$ of rank $k$. **Points-Lines-Planes conjecture.**

$$
W_2^2\geq\frac{3}{2}W_1W_3.
$$

This is a special case of conjectured log-concavity inequalities for the Whitney numbers of the second kind, with stronger inequalities attributed to Mason. The source gives no resolution of this rank-four case.
object.source_name: Eric Katz, “Matroid theory for algebraic geometers”, arXiv:1409.3503 (2014).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1409.3503

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of September 2014). “The characteristic polynomial of a matroid representable over a field of characteristic $0$ was proved to be strictly log-concave by Huh in by studying the variety of critical points that arises in maximum likelihood estimation.”

object.title: The strong cylinder conjecture in affine 3-space
object.statement:
Let $p$ be prime and let $U$ be a set of $p^2$ points in the affine space ${\rm AG}(3,p)$. **Strong cylinder conjecture.** If every plane meets $U$ in a number of points divisible by $p$, then $U$ is the union of $p$ parallel lines.
This strengthens the preceding cylinder conjecture by using the divisibility condition supplied by the direction theorem; the supplied text gives no resolution.
object.source_name: Jan De Beule, “Direction problems in affine spaces”, arXiv:1409.6960 (2014).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1409.6960

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2014).

object.title: The (I3) conjecture for path-transversal systems
object.statement: A **path-transversal system** is a system arising from path transversals in a dimaze. **The (I3) conjecture.** Any path-transversal system satisfies (I3). The preceding discussion notes that path-transversal systems need not satisfy (IM), and asks whether the weaker independence axiom (I3) always holds; its status is not resolved in the supplied text.
object.source_name: Seyed Hadi Afzali Borujeni, Hiu Fai Law and Malte Müller, “Infinite Gammoids: Minors and Duality”, arXiv:1411.2277 (2014).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1411.2277

Status: **open** according to the source (as of November 2014). “For easy reference for open problems, we list the following: Questions and , Conjectures and .”

object.title: The duality conjecture for $C^A$-free gammoids
object.statement: A **$C^A$-free gammoid** is a gammoid avoiding the excluded configuration $C^A$. **The duality conjecture.** The class of $C^A$-free gammoids is closed under duality. This is presented as an expected strengthening of the result that every $R^A$-free strict gammoid is dual to a gammoid; the supplied status evidence marks it as open.
object.source_name: Seyed Hadi Afzali Borujeni, Hiu Fai Law and Malte Müller, “Infinite Gammoids: Minors and Duality”, arXiv:1411.2277 (2014).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1411.2277

Status: **open** according to the source (as of November 2014). “For easy reference for open problems, we list the following: Questions and , Conjectures and .”

object.title: Jaikin-Zapirain's profinite conciseness conjecture
object.statement: Let $w$ be a group-word and $G$ a profinite group. Suppose that the set of $w$-values in $G$ is countable. **Profinite conciseness conjecture.** Then the verbal subgroup $w(G)$ is finite. The paper presents this as a conjecture in the context of relaxing the usual definition of conciseness for profinite groups; no resolution is given.
object.source_name: Cristina Acciarri and Pavel Shumyatsky, “Coverings of commutators in profinite groups”, arXiv:1511.07843 (2015).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1511.07843

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2015).

object.title: Second-range formula conjecture for the universal bound $g^*(r)$
object.statement:
Let $r\in\mathbb{Z}^{+}$, and suppose there exists $t\in\mathbb{Z}^{+}$ such that

$$
t(t+1)\leq r\leq (t+1)^2.
$$

**Second-range formula conjecture.** Then

$$
g^*(r)=\frac{2}{t+1}+\frac{1}{t}+\frac{r}{(t+1)^2}-\frac{r}{t(t+1)}.
$$

The formula is conjectured as part of the claimed optimality of the constructions in Theorems 7 and 8; no proof or resolution is supplied in the excerpt.
object.source_name: Charles Gong, “Minimizing Monochromatic Subgraphs of K_n,n”, arXiv:2410.19076 (2026).
object.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2014–2024). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1404.4339](https://arxiv.org/abs/1404.4339).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.19076

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2024).
